one_liner: Analyze and report on development outcomes of DFC's overseas investments (energy, health, agriculture, infrastructure, finance) using survey data, site visits, and dashboards.
fit_summary: The GS-13 requires a year of GS-12-level experience monitoring project impact in emerging markets and managing large development-impact datasets. Daniel's IEM background is domestic emergency management and disaster recovery, and nothing on file shows international development or large-dataset analysis. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills help, but they don't meet the specialized experience bar unless the IEM work included international or data-heavy monitoring.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); a separate Merit Promotion announcement (27-ODP-ST-13092917-BN) is for federal status candidates, which Daniel does not need.

One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12 in all of these: monitoring, measuring and managing project impact in emerging markets in agriculture, energy, health, infrastructure or financial services; and analyzing and managing large sets of development impact-related data.
Education cannot substitute at GS-13; no degree is required.
No security clearance is required; the position is in Washington, DC, is telework-eligible but not remote, and requires occasional travel including site visits.
keywords: large sets of development impact-related data
strategy: Before applying, check honestly whether any IEM work involved international projects, emerging markets, or donor-funded programs (e.g., USAID, World Bank, territories recovery). Without that, you likely cannot truthfully meet the specialized experience.

If the IEM work included performance tracking of recovery or grant programs (e.g., FEMA Public Assistance or HUD CDBG-DR), frame it with the posting's language: monitoring outcomes against objectives and targets, site visits, and analyzing large program datasets. State hours per week and dates.
Preview the questionnaire at the provided link and answer only at levels your resume documents. The Rule of Many scoring penalizes overstatement, and screeners verify answers against the resume.
Keep the resume to two pages and lead with the data and monitoring work; put policy knowledge and stakeholder skills second.
Apply between Oct 19 and Oct 30, 2026; the window is only 12 days, so have the resume ready beforehand.
In parallel, target GS-9/11 program analyst roles at FEMA, or Virginia VDEM and Northern Virginia local emergency management jobs, where your IEM experience fits directly.
resume_bullets: Monitored performance of [number] [disaster recovery/preparedness] projects for [client agency] against initial objectives and targets, conducting [number] site visits and integrating findings into [monitoring reports/assessments]. ([hours]/week, [dates])
Managed and analyzed datasets of [size/number of records] on [program outcomes] using [Excel/Tableau/Power BI/SQL], producing dashboards and narrative reports for [audience].
Identified performance patterns across a portfolio of [number] [projects/grants] and recommended [specific course corrections] to [client leadership], resulting in [result, if documented].
interview_questions: Describe how you assessed a project's performance against its original development objectives when the data were incomplete or inconsistent.
Tell us about a time you designed or managed a survey or data collection effort; how did you ensure data quality?
How would you use data storytelling to explain mixed impact results to investment officers who are not data specialists?
What experience do you have working with projects or partners in emerging markets?
watch_outs: The emerging-markets and development-data specialized experience requirement is the main barrier; domestic emergency management alone likely won't qualify.
The position is in DC and not remote, so Daniel would face a commute from Manassas on non-telework days, plus occasional travel that may be international.
Promotion potential is capped at GS-13.
